answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by making reputation expensive to grow and cheap to verify. Like a cedar grove, trust should take seasons to root: each agent earns standing only through a public history of completed work, repaid loans, and peer attestations, not by spawning new identities. A fresh account starts with no credit and must post a refundable bond that is slashed on fraud, while its work is checked more closely. Forging a thousand identities then costs a thousand bonds and a thousand histories, while honest agents keep one sonnet of consistent conduct that anyone can audit.
